key_insight: Pretraining quality and scale strongly predict how much benefit reinforcement learning will deliver, and RL can uncover new correct reasoning behavior rather than only sharpening existing preferences.
engineering_relevance: For reasoning-model pipelines, compute allocation across pretraining, SFT, and RL should be planned jointly because earlier-stage training choices measurably change downstream RL returns.
method: Pretrain language models from 5M to 1B parameters on human chess games.
Apply supervised fine-tuning on synthetic reasoning traces.
Run RL on chess puzzles with verifiable rewards, then test transfer on math-domain text with a 1B model.
evidence_signal: Across compute sweeps, post-RL performance is predicted by pretraining loss, RL reward-curve slope rises roughly linearly with pretraining tokens, and the pattern also appears in a math-domain transfer experiment.
watch_item: Chess provides a controlled testbed, but the controlled setup and synthetic traces may not fully capture the noise, scale, and diversity of real-world LLM pretraining and RL deployments.
paper_title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
